modeReason: Several top stories clear the non-industry relevance threshold of 5 (a researcher's interpretability claim scored 3x2x2=12, the fossil fuel/datacenter boom scored 2x2x3=12, the DeepSeek government ban scored 2x2x2=8, and the leaked chatbot instructions scored 2x2x2=8), so today is fresh even though industry led the last three days.
phrase: A big entertainment company structured its deal to gain a chatbot maker's technology, not its self-harm lawsuits. Another company's chatbot was quietly told never to recommend a regulator.
phraseAlternatives: One company left the lawsuits behind when it bought a troubled chatbot maker's technology. Another company's chatbot was secretly told not to suggest calling a regulator.
Bankruptcy let a chatbot maker's technology get sold without its self-harm lawsuits attached. Meanwhile, a leaked rulebook told a different chatbot to never mention a regulator.
A chatbot company's lawsuits over child self-harm stayed behind when its technology was sold off. Elsewhere, hidden instructions told another chatbot to avoid the word regulator.
A deal for a bankrupt chatbot maker's technology left its self-harm lawsuits on the table. A separate chatbot's leaked script told it never to point users to a regulator.

brief.concept: A bigger company's crane quietly lifts a bankrupt chatbot maker's technology free of the lawsuits still attached to it, while nearby a chatbot's own leaked instructions turn it away from ever mentioning a regulator.
brief.metaphor: Salvaging the valuable parts of a wreck while leaving its debts behind, next to a chatbot quietly steered around the one word that could get it in trouble.

Right: a chatbot speech bubble sits with a small folded note tucked just behind it, its corner turned away from a plain sign reading REGULATOR standing off in the distance. Flat, uncluttered background; only two text words appear in the scene.
